lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: Up the river, past the wheel, to the falls. There's a hollow in the rocks at the bottom.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: They go in at dawn. I hear them.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: Forty grosze. I'd say more. The wheel's been frozen two winters, I grind by hand what people bring, and nobody brings anything.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: I don't know. It doesn't turn. There's nothing in it for them.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: They sit there and then it snows in the yard. My wife will tell you.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: Mind the bank. The ice over the race is bad.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: I'll let the boy down to the river tomorrow. Not today.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: My father never let anyone fish there. Warm water comes up. The ice is never as thick as it looks.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: You put your hand in the hole there and it isn't cold like the other holes. My father did it, his father did it.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: The old ones know. Most of them are dead.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: There's soup, if you want. My wife made it.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: The boy's been down to the river twice. He took the dog's bowl with him.

lines.text: Wipe your feet. I've just done it.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: He did. He won't say it, but he hasn't slept.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Inside. They've been inside for six days. They fight.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Kill them, and you can have whatever is in the pot.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: I let them out into the yard this morning. They came back in covered in snow and I could have kissed them.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: There's soup. It's turnip, I'm sorry. It was turnip yesterday.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Soup's on, if you want it. Still turnip.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: They sit there from noon. Then it snows on the yard. Not on the hill, not on the wheel. The yard.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: On the line, on the step I've just swept. Gniewko says it's the same snow wherever it lands.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: His mother would have been out with the bell by now.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Gniewko's father had a hand-bell. Brass, about so big.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Every spring it would hail on the blossom, and he took it out to the ring on the last of the ice at dusk and rang it three times. They turned it off the orchard.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: The herders. They hear it and they go over. I don't know how it works. I only held the lamp.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: He left it out there the last good spring, tied to a pole so it would be to hand.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: He died the second winter. Nobody went for it.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Forty trees behind the house. Plum and apple. Not a leaf on them since the first winter.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: You'll say there's no sense in it.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Twenty grosze for the walk. It's what there is.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: Dusk, mind. Not before. Three times, and not a fourth.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: It's been out there two years.

lines.speaker: miller_wife
lines.text: It'll be on one of the poles. Look for the rag round the clapper. Dusk, mind.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Hunter! Over here, if you have a minute.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Up. I can't tie it from the ground.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Keep to that side. It's resting on the one runner and I don't trust it.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: The runner split at the knee. It went on the pass, I felt it go, and I've been dragging it since. I've rope and a mallet and I haven't got a third hand.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Still down. I'd be grateful for a pair of hands.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Pots, kettles, ladles. A hundred and some spoons. If I unload it I only have to load it again, and my back isn't the one I came with.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Marzena. I haven't been through in three years. Is Zbyszek still keeping the Bell?
lines.direction: plain, restrained; flat question, not rising

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.direction: plain, restrained; flat question, not rising

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Good. I've told people about that beer.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Take the corner by the load. Lift when I say and don't put it down till I've tied it off. It won't take long.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: That's the knee. It'll get me to the village, and I'll put a proper runner on there.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: I've no money to give you. I can sell you a Thaw draught for eight grosze. The tavern asks twelve.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: A woman at the foot of the pass makes them. I add a grosz for the carrying.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: I'll be by the stalls in the square, mornings, when it isn't snowing.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Pots mended, spoons, kettles. Thaw draught, eight grosze.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: You've three on you already. Come back when you've used one.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Eight grosze. I can't go lower, I pay seven.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: I'm out of the draughts. Pots, spoons, kettles, if you need them.

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.text: My Jasiek went up four days ago with the sledge, for wood. He's sixteen. I put the milk here for him, in case he comes by this way. It's no use to the shrine.

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.text: Tall. He stoops. A grey scarf with a red stripe, I knitted it, it's too long, he trips on it.

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.direction: plain, restrained; flat question, not rising

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.text: That's mine. I bought the wool off the Kowal woman.

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.direction: plain, restrained; after a held beat; short, quiet

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.text: I'll put it up on the post. He'll see it from the road.

lines.speaker: old_woman
lines.text: You'll want paying. It's eight grosze, it's what's in the jar. I'd rather it went somewhere.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: You came down the pass road. Did you see a goat? White, one ear folded over.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: She was through the fence yesterday. The wind drops it. She's never gone far, but there's nothing to eat out here and she'll have gone looking.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: Where it's green. There's nothing green. My husband says there's grass under the twisted pines past the marsh, a little, where the branches keep the snow off. Don't ask me how he knows.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: She bites. If you bring her back, there's three eggs, and they're not for anyone else.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.direction: plain, restrained; flat question, not rising

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: That's her. That's her, look. Come here. Come here, you stupid animal.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: Jan was right, then. He'll be unbearable.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: Three eggs, as I said. I'll not have it said I didn't pay.

lines.speaker: goat_owner
lines.text: She won't leave my side now. Jan wants to mend the fence. He's wanted to mend the fence since the autumn.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: It's not stuck. It's just stopped.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: It's the runner. It went in at the edge of the bank and now it won't come out. Mama says I have to be home with the wood before dark.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: There's none. And the reeve says leave the fences alone.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: It's still stuck. I mean stopped.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: You're the hunter. Ola says your eyes are just yellow.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: I've one grosz. Mama said if anybody helped I was to give them something.

lines.speaker: sled_boy
lines.text: I have to get this home.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: Nothing since dawn. They won't bite when it's clear.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: He's cut it too close to mine. I told him.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: I cut this hole. My father cut it before me, at this bend, every freeze.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: Your line is in my hole.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: You. Hunter. You've no stake in it. Say whose it is.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: Thirty winters I've cut that hole.

lines.speaker: fisher_old
lines.text: Mind the slush. It goes in the hole.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: He says my hole's too close to his. I say that's where the fish are.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: And I've been on it since before light. My line's in it.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: It's the river's hole. It's where the water comes in. Anyone can fish where the water comes in.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: The fish come where the river comes in. There's no sense cutting a hole where there's nothing.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: Of course. It's always the old ones' holes.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: Then I'll catch nothing somewhere else.

lines.speaker: fisher_young
lines.text: I'll cut it where I like.
